public_rationale: The independent planning evaluation documents a substantial increase in problems solved, including obfuscated problems on which earlier models performed very poorly. That exceeds faster output or additional input formats and meets the early-resolution rule. The improvement was neither universal nor reliable on every harder task, but the claim excludes substantial capability growth, not just flawless performance.
limitations: The planning study is a preprint and uses bounded benchmark tasks.
The researchers used GPT-4o-mini and a parser to normalise o1's output format.
Performance deteriorated on longer problems, and the study did not establish general intelligence.
The decisive date is the public report date, not an asserted date for individual test runs.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI cannot do much more than it currently does, beyond doing it faster with new inputs.

statement.excerpt: It cannot do much more than it is currently doing, other than doing more of it faster with some new inputs.

from_speaker: other than doing more of it faster
our_interpretation: The surrounding forecast language makes this an open-ended claim about a capability ceiling relative to July 8, 2024.
The plain reading excludes substantial gains in solving difficult tasks, not merely entirely new categories of task.
Language models trained to generate reasoning remain within generative AI.
Higher task-success rates can contradict the claim even if they require more computation; speed alone cannot.
criteria.support_condition: A demonstrated binding capability limit establishes that substantial further gains are impossible. A finite period without gains would not suffice.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A later system demonstrates substantial improvements on comparable substantive tasks beyond the July 2024 baseline, rather than only faster generation or additional input formats.

evidence.publisher: Valmeekam, Stechly, Gundawar and Kambhampati / arXiv
evidence.explanation: The public evaluation reported 97.8% success on basic Blocksworld and 52.8% on its obfuscated version, where earlier tested LLMs remained below 5%. These are substantive planning gains; the event date denotes publication of the demonstration, since exact test-run dates are not supplied.

ARC Prize found o1-preview approximately matched Claude 3.5 Sonnet's accuracy on its public evaluation while taking much longer. This limits the breadth of the improvement but does not negate the planning gains.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: Publication of an independent evaluation showing substantial planning-success gains beyond earlier systems, rather than only speed or new inputs.
